calculationNote: Typical $12,000: DFI $501.0 → building permit $501.0 + STFI plan review $200.4 (40% of DFI) + technology $35.07 (5%, SMC 22.900A.100) + WA BCC $6.50 (RCW 19.27.085) = $742.97 (Seattle SDCI 2026 Fee Subtitle Tables D-1 and D-2; STFI path: 100% building permit + 40% plan review of DFI; source retrieved 2026-08-13). Low $8,000 valuation = $648.89 total. That low band reconciles to whole-dollar DFI $437: building permit $437.00 (100% of DFI), plus STFI plan review $174.80 (40% of DFI), plus technology $30.59 (5% of the $611.80 permit and plan-review subtotal), plus WA BCC $6.50, equals $648.89. And high $22,000 valuation = $978.17 total. That high band reconciles to whole-dollar DFI $661: building permit $661.00 (100% of DFI), plus STFI plan review $264.40 (40% of DFI), plus technology $46.27 (5% of the $925.40 permit and plan-review subtotal), plus WA BCC $6.50, equals $978.17. Each recorded band is the STFI like-for-like reroof path. The rule is a building permit at 100% of DFI, plus plan review at 40% of DFI, times 1.05 for the technology fee, plus the flat $6.50 WA BCC. Alternate path not used in recorded totals: full plan review (200% of DFI) for structural changes or layered roofs when STFI is ineligible; confirm STFI eligibility with SDCI before filing.

sourceName: Seattle SDCI 2026 Fee Subtitle (SMC 22.900), Table D-8 (22.900D.090)
caveat: Like-for-like furnace/heat-pump swap is a mechanical equipment fee (Table D-8 / 22.900D.090), not the valuation DFI, using Seattle SDCI 2026 Fee Subtitle (retrieved 2026-08-13). Recorded bands: low 1 unit $60.35 × 1.05 tech → $63.37; typical 2 units 2 × $60.35 × 1.05 → $126.73; high 3 units 3 × $60.35 × 1.05 → $190.10 (SMC 22.900A.100 technology fee included). New duct systems submitted separately use Table D-2 (valuation) — that alternate path is not included in the recorded typical/low/high. Separate electrical (Table D-14 / OTC) is extra and null here.
calculationNote: Like-for-like furnace/heat-pump swap uses the Seattle SDCI 2026 Fee Subtitle (SMC 22.900) Table D-8 (22.900D.090) mechanical equipment fee, not the valuation DFI (source retrieved 2026-08-13). Table D-8 charges a fixed per-unit amount of $60.35 for each forced-air furnace, heat pump, or similar unit, including ducts attached thereto. The 5% technology fee under SMC 22.900A.100 is applied to that Table D-8 subtotal and is included in every recorded band. Low 1 unit is one forced-air furnace, heat pump, or similar unit, including ducts attached thereto: 1 × $60.35 = $60.35, plus the 5% technology fee $3.02 (SMC 22.900A.100), and $60.35 + $3.02 = $63.37. Typical 2 units (furnace + AC or two heat-pump outdoor/indoor): 2 × $60.35 Table D-8 = $120.70; the recorded 5% technology fee is $6.04 (SMC 22.900A.100); the recorded total is $126.73, which matches the recorded path 2 × $60.35 × 1.05. That $120.70 is the Mechanical equipment fee (Table D-8) extra on this row, and that $6.04 is the Technology fee (5%) extra; both are included in feeTypicalUsd, so they are not added again. High 3 units is three units on that same per-unit Table D-8 basis (forced-air furnace, heat pump, or similar, including ducts attached thereto): 3 × $60.35 = $181.05, plus the 5% technology fee $9.05 (SMC 22.900A.100), and $181.05 + $9.05 = $190.10. The low, typical, and high bands are therefore 1 × $60.35 × 1.05 → $63.37, 2 × $60.35 × 1.05 → $126.73, and 3 × $60.35 × 1.05 → $190.10. The per-unit charge covers ducts attached to that equipment; this row is not the Table D-2 valuation path. Excluded from these totals: a separate Table D-14 / OTC electrical permit if new circuits or disconnects, and new duct systems submitted separately, which use Table D-2 (valuation) instead of the Table D-8 per-unit mechanical equipment fee. Amounts for those alternates were not recorded as feeUsd lines. Confirm path with SDCI.

calculationNote: Typical $12,000: Tables D-1 and D-2 set DFI at $501.0 (Seattle SDCI 2026 Fee Subtitle, SMC 22.900; source retrieved 2026-08-13). On the recorded path the building permit is 100% of DFI and plan review is 100% of DFI. That is the full plan-review path: 100% building permit + 100% plan review of DFI, or 200% of DFI. Building plus plan review is the $1,002 building+plan subtotal. The technology fee is 5% of that $1,002. The WA State Building Code Council fee is a flat $6.50 when a building permit is issued, at low, typical, and high. Add the recorded pieces: DFI $501.0, building permit $501.0 + plan review $501.0 (100% of DFI) + technology $50.1 (5%, SMC 22.900A.100) + WA BCC $6.50 (RCW 19.27.085) = $1058.6. That is the recorded typical fee at the $12,000 typical project value. Low $8,000 valuation = $924.2 total ($437.0 building + $437.0 plan + $43.7 tech + $6.50 WA BCC). At $8,000 the DFI is $437.0. Building permit $437.0 plus plan review $437.0 is $874. Technology is 5% of $874, which is $43.7. Add the flat $6.50 WA BCC and the low total is $924.2. The high $19,200 valuation = $1300.52 total ($616.2 building + $616.2 plan + $61.62 tech + $6.50 WA BCC). At $19,200 the DFI is $616.2. Building permit $616.2 plus plan review $616.2 is $1,232.4. Technology is 5% of $1,232.4, which is $61.62. Add the flat $6.50 WA BCC and the high total is $1300.52. Recorded totals use that full plan review (200% of DFI), not the STFI 40% plan-review / ~140% of DFI path. Simple, prescriptive, or ground-level decks may qualify as STFI with ~140% of DFI (100% building permit + 40% plan review) instead of 200% of DFI. Alternate paths not used in recorded totals: STFI / simple-prescriptive / ground-level decks at ~140% of DFI (feeUsd null); decks under 30 inches above grade that may not need a building permit (feeUsd null). No separate STFI dollar total was recorded. Decks over 30 inches above grade generally need a building permit. A deck under 30 inches above grade may not need a building permit, and that path is not assumed in the recorded bands. These figures are the building-permit portion only. Confirm deck height, STFI eligibility, and current SDCI fees with SDCI before filing.

sourceName: N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(5); Mecklenburg County LUESA Fee Ordinance (revised July 1, 2026) Section II.A
caveat: Like-for-like replacement of existing roofing on a single-family dwelling costing $40,000 or less does not require a building permit under N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c) (addition of roofing is carved in; replacement is carved out). NC OSFM guidance (10/19/2023) reads the exemption as replacement of roofing plus up to 15% of existing roof deck. A permit is still required if cost exceeds $40,000, load-bearing structure is added/repaired/replaced beyond that deck allowance, or new roofing is added. If a permit is issued, LUESA Section II.A applies ($59.70 + $12.19/$1,000 over $3,000) plus a $3 technology charge.
calculationNote: The typical path is $0. N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(5) does not require a building permit for a like-for-like single-family reroof costing $40,000 or less. NC OSFM guidance (10/19/2023) reads that exemption as roofing replacement plus up to 15% of the existing roof deck. A permit is required when cost exceeds $40,000, when load-bearing work exceeds the OSFM deck allowance, or when new roofing is added. Walk the fee in three steps on the typical path. Step 1: confirm the job is a like-for-like single-family reroof at or under $40,000 with load-bearing work inside the OSFM deck allowance. Step 2: under N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(5), no building permit is required, so no LUESA Section II.A fee and no $3 technology charge apply. Step 3: the recorded low, typical, and high permit totals are therefore $0, $0, and $0. Alternate LUESA Section II.A applies only if a permit is issued, and only for projects not requiring plan review: $59.70 plus $12.19 per $1,000 or part over $3,000, plus a $3 technology charge (Note f). The recorded valuations on this row are low $8,000, typical $12,000, and high $22,000, and the recorded typical project value is $12,000. Low $8,000 is $5,000 over $3,000, which is 5 thousands: $59.70 + $12.19 x 5 = $120.65, then $120.65 + $3 = $123.65. Typical $12,000 is $9,000 over $3,000, which is 9 thousands: $59.70 + $12.19 x 9 = $169.41, then $169.41 + $3 = $172.41. High $22,000 is $19,000 over $3,000, which is 19 thousands: $59.70 + $12.19 x 19 = $291.31, then $291.31 + $3 = $294.31. The Valuation building permit extra of $169.41 is the Section II.A building fee at the $12,000 typical valuation before the technology charge, and the Technology charge extra of $3.00 is Note f. Those alternate totals, and those extras, are not included in the recorded $0 typical path. County LUESA totals only. Confirm with Mecklenburg County Code Enforcement if cost exceeds $40,000, load-bearing work exceeds the OSFM deck allowance, or new roofing is added. Source: N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(5); Mecklenburg County LUESA Fee Ordinance (revised July 1, 2026) Section II.A, retrieved 2026-08-29 (https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_160D/GS_160D-1110.html).

sourceName: Mecklenburg County LUESA Fee Ordinance (revised July 1, 2026), Section II.D.1 and Section II.A Note f
caveat: Replacement of heating/AC equipment requires a permit even under $40,000 (N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(3)). Recorded bands from Mecklenburg County LUESA Fee Ordinance (revised July 1, 2026), Section II.D.1 and Section II.A Note f (retrieved 2026-08-29): low single-trade mechanical $59.70 + $3 tech → $62.70; typical TIP two-trade change-out 1.5 × $59.70 + $3 → $92.55; high non-TIP path 2 × $79.61 + $3 → $162.22. N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(d)(1) caps some appliance-replacement building permits at one trade permit; confirm TIP eligibility with Code Enforcement — the non-TIP high path is not included when TIP applies.
calculationNote: Low single-trade is the recorded low band when a homeowner files only one trade and there is no second trade. That path uses the Section II.A minimum for projects not requiring plan review. The arithmetic is $59.70 + $3 tech = $62.70. A typical heating and cooling change-out on a single-family home or townhouse needs two trade permits, mechanical plus electrical or plumbing, filed through Trades Internet Permit. That situation is the Typical TIP two-trade change-out under LUESA Section II.D.1. The arithmetic is 1.5 × $59.70 = $89.55, then $89.55 + $3 = $92.55. The $3.00 technology charge applies once per permit, and TIP counts as one permit (Section II.A Note f), so the $3.00 is included once in the low, once in the typical, and once in the high. It is not charged once for each trade. High non-TIP is the recorded high band when TIP is not available. That path uses the ordinance maximum permit fee in Section II.D.1, read from the commercial-with-plan-review minimum. The arithmetic is 2 × $79.61 = $159.22, then $159.22 + $3 = $162.22. Replacement of heating or air-conditioning equipment requires a permit even under $40,000 (N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(c)(3)). N.C.G.S. 160D-1110(d)(1) caps some appliance-replacement building permits at one trade permit, and the non-TIP high path is not included when TIP applies. These bands come from the Mecklenburg County LUESA Fee Ordinance revised July 1, 2026, Sections II.D.1 and II.A, retrieved 2026-08-29. Alternate path not used in the recorded typical: the low single-trade filing and the high non-TIP filing are separate situations, and they are not stacked on top of the typical. Amounts beyond the recorded low and the recorded high were not added as new fee lines. Confirm TIP eligibility with Mecklenburg County Code Enforcement.

It is already inside each total and is not added again. Low $8,000 = $245.69 total. That is 6 additional thousands: $89.45 + $22.95 x 6 = $227.15. $227.15 + $18.54 = $245.69. Two extras are recorded, and both extras are included in the totals: the Application fee is $25, and the note on that extra is Included; the Building permit fee is $120, and the note on that extra is Included. $10 per $1,000 or fraction over $3,000. sourceName: City of Tacoma residential permits (IRC R105.2 / TMC 2.02.540 exemptions) and PDS Fee Schedule Table 8-1 effective January 1, 2026
caveat: City of Tacoma, not Seattle and not unincorporated Pierce. Official exemption: reroofing of SFR/duplex when existing coverings are removed, new roofing does not exceed 2.5 psf (or a previously approved same-weight vegetated roof), no roof-framing changes, and the building is not unreinforced masonry. Typical asphalt strip-and-reroof is the documented path. Overlay without tear-off is a separate OTC/ePermit and is not this typical.
calculationNote: Typical path = $0 (official asphalt strip-and-reroof exemption for the City of Tacoma, not Seattle and not unincorporated Pierce; IRC R105.2 and TMC 2.02.540; source retrieved 2026-09-01). The IRC R105.2 and TMC 2.02.540 exemption covers reroofing of a single-family home or a duplex when the existing roof coverings are removed before the new roofing goes on. The new roofing material does not exceed 2.5 psf (2.5 pounds per square foot). A vegetated roof is the other recorded weight path only when it is the same weight as the previous roof and a vegetated roof was previously approved through a building permit. No changes are made to roof framing. The building is not unreinforced masonry. A typical asphalt strip-and-reroof that meets those conditions is the documented path on this row. Recorded fee low, typical, and high stay $0 / $0 / $0. Those three zeros are the published exemption under IRC R105.2 and TMC 2.02.540, not a blank schedule and not a valuation-table lookup. Recorded assumed valuations are low $8,000, typical $12,000, and high $22,000. The recorded typical project value is $12,000. Those figures are the cost-model job bands. They do not change the $0 / $0 / $0 permit fees, because this row does not price the IRC R105.2 exemption from a valuation table. Overlay without tear-off is a separate OTC/ePermit and is not this typical. The residential permits page lists roof overlay as an over-the-counter residential alteration when a pre-inspection is completed, and as an ePermit for installation over no more than one existing layer with no structural or pitch change. That overlay path is not the strip-and-reroof exemption, and this row does not invent a fee for it. No extra fee lines are recorded on this row. The cited schedule name includes the PDS Fee Schedule effective January 1, 2026. Table 8-1 on that schedule prices other building permits on valuation. This roof row does not apply Table 8-1 dollars to the IRC R105.2 exemption. Confirm the IRC R105.2 and TMC 2.02.540 exemption, tear-off, the 2.5 psf limit, framing, and unreinforced masonry with City of Tacoma Planning and Development Services (PDS) before you start work.
